description: Migrate a Node.js authentication service from CommonJS to ES Modules. The project is located at /home/ga/workspace/auth-service/ and contains 4 JavaScript files and a package.json that need migration. TASK REQUIREMENTS: (1) Add '"type": "module"' to package.json to enable ES Modules. (2) Convert ALL require() statements to import statements in all .js files: src/auth.js, src/utils/hash.js, src/config.js, and test/auth.test.js. For built-in Node.js modules like 'crypto', 'fs', 'path', use the 'node:' prefix (e.g., 'import crypto from "node:crypto"'). For local modules, convert 'const X = require("./file")' to 'import X from "./file.js"' (note: add .js extension). For named imports, convert 'const { a, b } = require("./file")' to 'import { a, b } from "./file.js"'. (3) Convert ALL module.exports to export statements: 'module.exports = X' becomes 'export default X', and 'module.exports = { a, b }' becomes 'export { a, b }' or individual 'export function a() {}' statements. (4) In src/config.js, handle the JSON import properly using either: import syntax with assert (e.g., 'import config from "../config.json" assert { type: "json" }') OR fs.readFileSync with import.meta.url. (5) If __dirname or __filename are used, replace them with ESM equivalents using import.meta.url and fileURLToPath from 'node:url'. (6) Save all modified files. The verifier will check that package.json has '"type": "module"', that no require() or module.exports statements remain in the source code (comments excluded), that all files use import/export syntax, and that the JSON configuration is loaded in an ESM-compatible way.
